blogPosts.title: What Your Weekly Averages Actually Tell You
blogPosts.excerpt: Why tracking the right numbers matters more than tracking more numbers.
blogPosts.author: Noah Patel
content: Most people tracking weight loss are drowning in daily data points that don't mean much on their own — a single day's weight is mostly noise.
What matters is the 7-day rolling average, resting heart rate trend, and whether your strength numbers are holding steady while the scale moves.
A good deficit paired with resistance training should show a downward weight trend while your lifts stay flat or improve slightly — that's the signal you actually want.
If your lifts are dropping fast, your deficit is too aggressive. Data doesn't lie, even when the mirror does.

sections.heading: Information we collect
sections.body: We collect account information, membership details, and training data captured by connected equipment during your sessions.

sections.heading: How we use it
sections.body: Your training data is used solely to power your progress dashboard and inform your coach's programming. We do not sell member data to third parties.

sections.heading: Your rights
sections.body: You can export or delete your training data at any time from your dashboard settings, or by asking a coach.

sections.heading: Membership terms
sections.body: Memberships are billed monthly and can be cancelled with 30 days notice.

sections.heading: Equipment use
sections.body: Connected equipment logs training data automatically; members may opt out of data logging for individual sessions at the front desk.

sections.heading: Liability
sections.body: Exercise carries inherent risk. Members are responsible for training within their own limits and consulting a physician before starting a new program if needed.
